WhatsApp preps travel eSIM discovery, installation, and management tools

WhatsApp could soon be your one-stop shop for all things eSIM.

•

•

•

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• WhatsApp appears to be developing a system for eSIM discovery, purchase, installation, and management.

• Users would be able to search for eSIMs based on specific travel destinations.

• Automated tools could wait to activate the eSIM until you arrive where you’re headed.

WhatsApp just got a big upgrade with the announcement of support for scheduling messages, and now we’re already getting an early look at what could be coming next, as we uncover evidence for what looks like a new travel eSIM feature.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Looking across the changes present in WhatsApp’s version 2.26.47.10 update, we’re finding multiple references to “Travel eSIM” support. This isn’t yet live in the app, but here’s a preview for how one of the associated screens could be taking shape:

AssembleDebug / Android Authority

Internally, we’re seeing a whole lot of text strings that appear connected to this feature. Here are just a few:

Code

+Travel eSIM installed
+Keep WhatsApp open until it’s done.
+Installing travel eSIM…
+Getting your travel eSIM ready…
+Install it once and use with all your plans.
+Your travel eSIM is ready
+WhatsApp will add a travel eSIM to your phone. Your plan starts when your phone connects in %1$s.
+Install eSIM?
+This phone can’t take this eSIM. It may be locked to a carrier or out of eSIM space.
+Couldn’t install travel eSIM
+This eSIM’s activation code is invalid or has already been used.
+Couldn’t set up your travel eSIM
+Travel eSIMs aren’t available to you yet
+Your plan starts when you turn on your eSIM.
+Couldn’t load plans
+Loading data plans
+Plans aren’t available for this destination
+Your phone didn’t let WhatsApp install this eSIM.
+Installing an eSIM needs a phone with an eSIM chip and a recent version of Android.
+This phone can’t install eSIMs
+Install it now and turn it on when you arrive in %1$s.
+Your plan starts when your phone connects there. You’ll get a message when it does.

Based on what we’ve found so far, we can make a few guesses about how this is likely to operate. It seems that we’ll be able to enter a destination into the app, and WhatsApp would search for compatible eSIM options. Those may not be available for everyone, all at once, as we find “coming soon” messages prepared for both global and regional plans. Options may include fixed-data, as well as unlimited plans.

You can expect to see a few introductory screens helping to educate users about eSIMs, and it sure looks like the app is preparing to integrate with Android’s eSIM installation process.

One handy feature could be an automated system for turning on the eSIM only when we actually reach the destination we intended to use it — freeing us from accidentally plowing through our eSIM data before we really needed it.

Management tools should let you view the eSIMs you’ve purchased so far, seeing which are still available, which are expired, and which have data remaining on them. And along the way, it looks like the app will be able to give you low-data warnings or let you know when a plan is about to end.

Readers' poll

Would you use WhatsApp to buy and install eSIMs?

0 votes

Of course, there’s the possibility your phone may not support this functionality, especially if it’s running an older version of Android. For the moment, at least, we don’t yet have a clear sense for where that cutoff may lie, but expect there to be one.

Finally, WhatsApp might not be preparing this new support on its own, and a “Powered by %1$s” string could suggest that some of this eSIM system may arrive courtesy of a third-party service — we just don’t yet know whose name is going to show up in place of that variable.

All of this sounds pretty nice to our ears. Buying an eSIM is a great option for international travel, and WhatsApp is a great messaging service for travel abroad, so this feels like a match made in heaven. It also looks like WhatsApp is serious about its approach here, and the strings we’ve found paint the picture of quite robust integration. For now, we’ll keep looking for the rest of the details on how this new service offering could be coming together.

On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account…
items.body: Popular password management app 1Password today said it experienced a security breach earlier this month. 1Password says some customer names and email addresses were accessed, but no customer vault contents were compromised. On November 19, 1Password saw indications that an employee's GitHub account had been breached and began investigating. The company says the breached GitHub account was used to access source code and push malicious code to backend services, with the code downloading some customer data. Here's a list of what the hacker was able to get: Names and email addresses customers use to sign into 1Password Account and user identifiers, and account creation and last sign-in times Public keys Secure Remote Password protocol parameters (1Password says this can't be used for account access) Tokens in emailed links for invitations, provisioning, and account recovery Other non-secret account data related to 1Password's internal architecture, like version numeric identifiers and file numeric identifiers 1Password source code, which 1Password says does not include customer data or user secrets Access to 1Password's CI/CD system, which it says has infrastructure-related secrets for the service to work According to 1Password, there is no impact to its services, availability, or product security. Customer vaults and the items in them were not accessed, nor were the keys that protect vaults. The hacker did not have access to account recovery keys or 1Password apps and browser extensions. 1Password vaults are encrypted and protected by keys on the user end, so content is not accessible to 1Password or anyone who hacks the 1Password servers. The biggest risk comes from the token breach. Tokens can be used for account recovery, but they only work when paired with an SSO sign-in or a six-digit code sent to a user's email address. items.title: WhatsApp Finally Adds Scheduled Messages
items.summary: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a messag…
items.body: Popular messaging app WhatsApp was today updated with an option to schedule messages, which the company says was one of its most requested features. WhatsApp users can create a message and schedule it to arrive from 10 minutes to 14 days later in one-to-one chats and group chats. Scheduling a message can be done by pressing and holding the send button after composing and then choosing a date and time. Scheduled messages work with text, photos, and videos, and will still send even if a user's device is offline. There is an option to see all scheduled messages and delete them before they're sent if needed. Scheduled messages are end-to-end encrypted and look like any other WhatsApp message, with no indication on the receiver's end that the message was scheduled. Apple's iMessage service already has a Send Later feature that supports scheduling messages, so WhatsApp is catching up with Apple's built-in messaging option. WhatsApp says scheduled messages are rolling out globally over the coming weeks. items.summary: Everyday voice commands should feel a little less frustrating.
items.body:

Smart home

Gemini for Home gets faster responses, smoother chats, and fixes for follow-up and music bugs

Everyday voice commands should feel a little less frustrating.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 3:15 PM ET

•

•

Joe Maring / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Google has fully rolled out speed improvements for common Gemini for Home smart home commands.

• The latest update fixes bugs affecting follow-up commands and stopping media playback.

• Google is also rolling out an improved Gemini Live experience, more expressive storytelling, and web answer sources on supported smart displays.

The story of Gemini for Home’s transition from Google Assistant is beginning to take a more positive turn. We’ve seen some users warming up to Google’s new voice assistant, particularly after noticeable improvements in response times. Now, Google is giving Gemini more polish, whether you’re asking it to switch off the lights or tell your kids a bedtime story.

With its second November update, Google has confirmed that speed improvements for common smart home commands have fully rolled out to Gemini for Home Early Access users. So, whether you’re turning on the lights or adjusting the thermostat, Gemini should respond and act faster.

Google has also fixed a bug where Gemini would occasionally forget the context of a conversation. For example, asking Gemini to turn the living room lights back on shortly after telling it to turn them off should now work as expected. Another fix addresses an issue where Gemini would incorrectly insist that nothing was playing when asked to stop music or other media.

Brady Snyder / Android Authority

Beyond these fixes, Google is beginning to roll out the upgraded Gemini Live experience it announced last week alongside energy-saving improvements for Nest thermostats and new features for Google Home cameras. Over the coming weeks, Google Home Premium subscribers will get faster, more natural conversations with Gemini, along with the ability to set timers, add reminders, and control smart home devices without ending an ongoing chat.

Gemini is also becoming a better storyteller. Starting today, stories will feature more expressive voices and varied pacing, and you can steer the plot as Gemini narrates. And if you own a supported smart display, you’ll be able to tap a new “Sources” option to see the websites Gemini used to answer your questions.

With Google Assistant set to retire from smart home devices in August 2027, every little improvement counts. And while more entertaining bedtime stories are a welcome addition, getting Gemini to remember which lights you were talking about is likely to make a bigger difference in everyday life.

Rumor: iOS 28 to Revamp Notifications

Wednesday November 25, 2026 11:58 am PST by Joe Rossignol

Earlier today, we resurfaced a longstanding issue with Apple not consistently enforcing its rules related to iPhone apps advertising through notifications. It is a good time to share that we heard from multiple sources that Apple is planning to revamp the iPhone's notification system with iOS 28 next year.

The sources said iOS 28 will include significant changes to Notification Center, but we do not have any specific details. This is just a rumor. On Android 16 and later, you can filter notifications into News, Promotions, Social, and Suggested categories, and an equivalent iOS option if implemented would help to hide advertising clutter.

items.title: The tiny $449 enough phone just got a huge battery, storage, and RAM upgrade
items.summary: Crowdfunders will get 50% more RAM, double the storage, and a beefier silicon-carbon battery.
items.body:

Mobile

The tiny $449 enough phone just got a huge battery, storage, and RAM upgrade

Crowdfunders will get 50% more RAM, double the storage, and a beefier silicon-carbon battery.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 2:46 PM ET

•

•

enough phone

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• The enough phone is trying to offer a throwback Android experience with its 5.3-inch display and compact, pocket-friendly build.

• When first announced earlier this month, the phone was set to get 8GB of RAM, 128GB storage, and a 3,500mAh battery.

• Instead of that, it will now ship with 12GB of RAM, 256GB storage, and a 3,850mAh silicon-carbon battery.

In 2026, we’ve all started getting used to the idea of phones trying to do more with less, as RAM and chip shortages impact production everywhere, but one upstart is now bucking that trend, as the tiny enough phone scores a surprise spec upgrade.

We first heard of the enough phone earlier this month. The crowdfunded handset was envisioned as a response to design trends that have pushed smartphones into larger and larger territory, prompting its creators to instead go with a 5.3-inch screen that’s much smaller than what you’ll find on the vast majority of handsets out there.

Priced at $449 over on Kickstarter at its current early bird level (the $399 level is already sold out), the handset was initially announced as running a Dimensity 7500 SoC, paired with 8GB of RAM, 128GB internal storage, and getting its power from a 3,500mAh battery — nothing really spectacular there, but what felt like some decent compromises to keep costs down.

With eight days left to go on its crowdfunding effort, enough is now sharing some big upgrades to those specs — and without any change to pricing. Instead of 8GB, the phone will now be equipped with 12GB of RAM. Storage is also getting a boost, climbing from 128GB to 256GB — and that’s even expandable, an all-too-rare feature these days.

Finally, enough is giving the phone a beefier battery. Rather than 3,500mAh, the phone will ship with a 3,850mAh battery. While a 10% boost may not sound like much, enough is also committing to giving the phone a silicon-carbon battery. That should help save space internally, as well as support speedier charging.

Right now, the enough phone is about 85% of the way towards reaching its crowdfunding goal, and the company says it needs roughly 100 more backers to sign on to reach its target. Once that’s over, the final retail price will rise to $599. If anyone out there was on the fence, do these upgrades finally push you over? Let us know down in the comments.

WhatsApp catches up to Google Messages with scheduling for texts, photos, and videos

Messages can be set 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time.

TL;DR

• WhatsApp now lets you schedule messages 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time in individual and group chats.

• The feature works with texts, photos, and video in both one-on-one and group chats.

• Competitors Google Messages, Signal, and Telegram have had scheduled messages for a while.

Lots of things can keep you from being a reliable texter, including thinking of the right thing to say but at the wrong time, and WhatsApp is now able to help out with that by adding support for scheduled messages.

Today, the messaging app announced that it’s adding the ability for users to schedule messages to send at a future point. WhatsApp says this has been one of the features that users requested most. Scheduled messaging was already available on Google Messages, Signal, and Telegram, so it finally brings WhatsApp up to speed with the competition.

WhatsApp

WhatsApp users can set a message to send from 10 minutes to 14 days ahead of time. The feature works with texts, photos, and video in both one-on-one and group chats, and the messages are end-to-end encrypted. The recipient won’t receive any indication that a message has been scheduled.

Scheduled messages are handy for more than making sure not to miss sending birthday greetings on the right day or to avoid waking someone up for just a meme when they’re in another time zone. Because messages are sent even if a user’s phone is off or out of battery at the scheduled time, the feature is also useful for when you know you’ll be unreachable, like when traveling.

WhatsApp said that scheduled messages are rolling out globally starting today. The timing should make it much easier to manage the upcoming holiday season, when sending out greetings can quickly go from heartwarming to overwhelming.

Once you have access to scheduled messages, you can draft a message as usual and then press and hold the send button and pick the date and time you want it to arrive. WhatsApp notes that you can see all of your scheduled messages in your account, and you can delete them before they’re set to send if you change your mind.

items.body: Hong Kong startup Savage Technology has announced its first product, "Orrorin Glasses," promising Vision Pro-style pinch controls and full-color displays for both eyes in a frame weighing just 45 grams. The company describes the glasses as offering "Vision Pro–level interaction" and being around 25 times lighter than Apple's headset, including its external battery. Savage highlights the bulky hardware currently required for Apple's spatial computing experience, although Orrorin offers substantially fewer capabilities. Savage says small pinches performed at the user's side control the interface without a ring, wristband, or controller. Eye tracking makes the display fade when the wearer looks away, rather than selecting interface elements as it does on Vision Pro. That also distinguishes Orrorin from the Meta Ray-Ban Display, which costs the same $799 but has a screen for only the right eye and requires a Neural Band wristband for gesture control. Standard Ray-Ban Meta glasses have no displays. Orrorin lacks positional tracking and spatial mapping , so it cannot anchor virtual windows in a room like Vision Pro. Orrorin is the first product from Savage Technology, co-founded by Bill Pei and Elena Shi, and remains in engineering validation for now. The company is currently targeting developers with third-party apps and interaction with AI agents such as Claude Code and Codex. Apple is expected to launch its first smart glasses next year , although the initial model reportedly will not have displays, instead offering speakers, microphones, and Siri integration. Orrorin reservations start at $29 toward the $799 price. Savage estimates shipments will begin in March 2027 for Founder Edition buyers and May 2027 for Early Bird buyers. items.body: Apple has rules in place that are supposed to protect iPhone users from unwanted advertising in push notifications and Live Activities, but some apps appear to be flouting these rules, and Apple does not appear to be consistently enforcing them. Apple's App Store guidelines do allow iPhone apps to send push notifications for promotions or direct marketing purposes, but only if users have "explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed" in the app, and so long as the app provides a method "for a user to opt out from receiving such messages." The guideline, in part: Push Notifications should not be used for promotions or direct marketing purposes unless customers have explicitly opted in to receive them via consent language displayed in your app's UI, and you provide a method in your app for a user to opt out from receiving such messages. Unfortunately, there are some examples of apps ignoring this guideline. On my iPhone in Canada, there are several apps that send me push notifications containing promotions without offering a way to opt out of these promotion-specific notifications, such as Cineplex, McDonald's, and Wendy's. Based on what we know so far, the Ear note will record calls through both the earbuds and the charging case, with the latter featuring a couple of handy buttons to start recording instantly. The companion app can turn all recordings into summaries and transcripts, with support for Nothing’s AI voice assistant alongside other AI agents.

Pricing information is currently unavailable, and that’s unlikely to change until the company announces the Ear note on December 8.

Nothing released the Ear 3a earlier this year with audio and call recording support. However, the Ear note takes it a step further with its charging case that serves as a standalone audio recorder.

items.summary: You can ask Gemini or Perplexity, but only Perplexity answers automatically.
items.body:
Affiliate links on Android Authority may earn us a commission. Learn more.

Mobile

Samsung quietly expands Modes and Routines with AI and 7 presets in One UI 9.5

You can ask Gemini or Perplexity, but only Perplexity answers automatically.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 10:06 AM ET

•

•

Adamya Sharma / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• One UI 9.5 Beta 1 adds an “Ask AI assistant” action to Samsung’s Modes and Routines app that can send prompts to Gemini or Perplexity.

• In our testing, Perplexity automatically sends prompts and reads answers aloud hands-free, whereas Gemini only prefills the prompt and waits for a manual tap because the Google app blocks Samsung’s auto-send request.

• The update also unlocks text summarization, offline translation, image text extraction, and a Repeat loop action. There are also seven new preset routines, including a Morning news briefing that only works hands-free when switched to Perplexity.

Samsung’s Modes and Routines has quietly become one of the most useful parts of One UI for power users. It lets you automate almost anything on your Galaxy phone with simple “if this, then that” rules. With the One UI 9.5 beta, Routines can now hand tasks to an AI assistant as well. Samsung didn’t mention this in the One UI 9.5 beta changelog, but we tried it on our Galaxy S26 Ultra, and which AI assistant you pick makes a big difference.

APK teardown

This reporting is based on work-in-progress code. These features may not ship.

You're reading an Android Authority exclusive story you won’t find anywhere else. An APK teardown helps predict features that may arrive on a service in the future based on work-in-progress code. However, it is possible that such predicted features may not make it to a public release. More Authority Insights →

Routines can now ask Gemini or Perplexity for you

Modes and Routines v5.2.00.69 in One UI 9.5 Beta 1 adds a new action called “Ask AI assistant.” You pick an assistant, type a prompt into the “Enter command” box, and the routine sends it whenever its trigger fires, whether that’s dismissing your alarm, arriving at work, or tapping a button. The prompt can also include text from earlier actions in the routine, going up to 8,000 characters.

Gemini and Perplexity are the only two options for Ask AI assistant, and they appear only if their apps are installed. Both are built into the Routines app, so you can’t add other AI assistants like ChatGPT or Claude. Routines still has a separate “Ask Bixby” action from One UI 9, too.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

There’s a catch, though: Routines can only launch the assistant. It doesn’t wait for an answer or receive one from the assistant, so you can’t feed the AI’s response back into a later action like a pop-up or a note. The routine finishes as soon as the assistant opens.

Perplexity answers on its own, but Gemini waits for you

With Perplexity, Routines opens the app’s floating assistant with the prompt and tells it to send the prompt right away:

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

In our testing, once the routine was triggered, Perplexity searched the web, answered in its overlay with sources, and read the answer aloud, without us touching the phone.

Gemini is a different story, though. Routines first tries to send the prompt automatically through a Google app service. If that fails, it falls back to sharing the text with the Gemini app, which only prefills the prompt.

On our Galaxy S26 Ultra, the Google app (v17.76.14) rejected Samsung’s request, so Routines used the fallback. Gemini opened full screen with our prompt typed in, and then waited for us to tap Send (which kind of defeats the convenience of a routine).

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Seemingly, the Google app only lets Google’s own apps use this service (for now), so Samsung’s automation has to stop halfway. Google could add Samsung Routines to that allowlist before One UI 9.5’s stable release. Until then, Perplexity is the only assistant that works hands-free in a routine. This is a nice win for Samsung’s growing partnership with Perplexity, even though the limitation likely comes from Google’s side.

The new Morning news briefing preset doesn’t work as advertised with Gemini

This disparity in auto-send behavior in Perplexity vs Gemini matters most for one of the seven new preset routines. “Morning news briefing” runs when you dismiss your alarm, and Samsung describes it like this:

Code

<string name="preset_name_morning_news">Morning news briefing</string>
<string name="preset_description_morning_news">When you dismiss your alarm, a summary of the latest news in society, business, and the stock market is read aloud.</string>
<string name="preset_param_morning_news">Summarize today's top news in 2-3 highlights for society, business, and the stock market.</string>

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

However, the preset’s only action is Ask AI assistant, and it’s set to Gemini by default. There’s no separate read-aloud step in the preset. As a result, with Gemini, you’ll dismiss your alarm and find the news prompt sitting unsent in Gemini. Nothing gets read back to you automatically.

When you switch the assistant to Perplexity, you get the spoken briefing Samsung promises.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Routines also learns to summarize, translate, and read text from images

The One UI 9.5 beta also adds several more actions:

• “Summarize text” condenses text from earlier in the routine. It runs on Samsung’s servers and needs a Samsung account. It also won’t work if you’ve turned on “Process data only on device” for Galaxy AI, except for the Timeline style.

• “Translate text” runs entirely on your phone using Samsung’s offline language packs.

• “Extract text from image” reads text from a picture, such as your latest screenshot.

• “Repeat” loops actions in a routine.

Summarize and Translate existed in One UI 9’s Routines app, but were hidden and not accessible to users. One UI 9.5 makes them available to everyone.

These actions power some of the new presets. “Screenshot translation,” for example, extracts text from your screenshot, translates it, and shows the result in a pop-up. In One UI 9.5 Beta 1, though, the preset can’t be saved because its “Screen captured” trigger isn’t active yet. When we rebuilt it with a manual trigger, it translated a Settings screenshot into Hindi in a couple of seconds, entirely on the device.

Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority

Seven new preset routines are ready to use in the One UI 9.5 Beta 1

One UI 9.5 adds seven new preset routines in total, which you’ll find under Discover > New preset routines:

• Pomodoro timer: Get notified at the start of each 25-minute focus session followed by a 5-minute break.

• Monthly media cleanup: Once a month, your duplicate photos and old media files are shown for you to review and delete.

• Screenshot translation: When a screenshot is taken, text from the image is translated and shown in a pop-up.

• Morning news briefing: When you dismiss your alarm, a summary of the latest news in society, business, and the stock market is read aloud.

• Meeting recorder: A meeting is recorded, transcribed, and summarized, then saved as a note with the date and time.

• Plank workout routine: Get a voice guide for three sets of 1-minute planks and rest intervals.

• Monthly storage cleanup: Once a month, your old download files, installation files, and unused apps are shown for you to review and delete.

Samsung hasn’t mentioned any of these Routines changes in its One UI 9.5 beta changelog, but they’re already live in the beta, so you can try them if you’ve installed it. Things could still change before the stable release, especially if Google lets Routines automatically send prompts to Gemini. If you’re on the beta, try the Morning news briefing preset with Perplexity, and let us know in the comments below how it works for you.

The offers will change, and new ones will launch, so we’ll keep updating this page regularly. Bookmark it to check back on what Black Friday deals are available.

Keep in mind that some of the best Black Friday deals on Amazon are only available to Prime members. If you’re not a member yet, you can usually sign up for a free 30-day trial, which you can cancel at any time. That way, you won’t miss out on any Prime-exclusive savings. Hit the button below to start your free trial.

The best Black Friday deals 2026

SPONSORED

Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds — $99 ($30 off)

Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds

Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds

The Timekettle LiveTalk earbuds are AI-powered translation earbuds designed for real-time multilingual conversations, helping users communicate across language barriers during meetings, travel, and everyday interactions.

See price at Amazon

Save $30.00

Black Friday deal: $99 (23% off) until November 30 for Prime members on Amazon.

The Timekettle LiveTalk AI Translation Earbuds work like a real-time interpreter, with a lightweight, open-ear design made for all-day comfort. You can enjoy music, listen to podcasts, and take calls as usual, then switch to translation whenever you need to chat with someone in another language. The comfortable ear-hook design rests outside your ear canal so you can stay aware of your surroundings. And at just 6.9 g each, they’re easy to wear all day.

Timekettle

LiveTalk in the Timekettle app features four handy modes, each designed for a different situation. Face-to-Face Translation helps with two-way conversations, whether each person wears one earbud or one person uses the earbuds while the other speaks through the phone app. And AI Translation Refinement helps make translated sentences sound more natural.

For one-way speech, like lectures, guided tours, or presentations, Live Listening displays a live transcript on your phone and generates real-time AI summaries, helping you quickly review key points as the speaker talks. Voice Call Translation works with both regular and internet calls, while Multimedia Translation makes it easier to follow foreign-language videos, podcasts, and online courses.

LiveTalk supports 54 languages and 108 accents, and it even includes 25 free offline translation packages for flights, remote areas, or when you want to avoid roaming charges.Besides translation, these earbuds are useful for daily use, with customizable EQ settings and the ability to connect to your phone and laptop at the same time. Each charge gives you up to four hours of active translation.

Timekettle is known for its AI translation devices, and LiveTalk is its lighter and more affordable option for everyday use. It’s a good choice for travelers, language learners, multilingual families, or students going abroad next semester.

For Black Friday, Amazon Prime members can get the Timekettle LiveTalk for just $99 (23% off) through November 30.

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL for $899

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL

Google Pixel 11 Pro XL

The top Pixel

The Google Pixel 11 Pro XL is a premium Android flagship powered by Tensor G6, with a 6.8-inch 1-120Hz Super Actua display, upgraded triple cameras with 120x Pro Zoom, a 5,115mAh battery, Pixelsnap Qi2.2 charging, and seven years of updates.

See price at Amazon

Save $400.00

Black Friday deal: $899 at Amazon (save $400).

Google’s biggest non-folding flagship is $400 off at Amazon, its lowest price yet. The Pixel 11 Pro XL brings Google’s top camera system, a large high-end display and the latest Gemini features. It also gets years of guaranteed updates, which makes it a strong long-term buy at this price.

SPONSORED

Narwal Flow 2 Robot Vacuum & Mop — $949.99 ($550 off)

Narwal Flow 2

Narwal Flow 2

Big suction power and powerful mopping features

The Narwal Flow 2 delivers massive suction power, excellent mops, nearly-perfect hair anti-tangle strategies, and maximum maintenance free operation. AI-powered navigation is reliable, a solid whole-home cleaning experience.

See price at Narwal

Save $550.00

Black Friday deal: $949.99 (save $550).

We were already big fans of the Narwal Flow 2 before this superb Black Friday deal came along. It earned an Editor’s Choice award in our review thanks to its excellent cleaning performance, smart navigation, and hands-off convenience. It’s not cheap at its $1,499.99 retail price, but this deal makes it a much more tempting prospect. Narwal’s 2026 flagship has dropped to just $949.99 at both Narwal and Amazon, saving you a hefty $550.

Edgar Cervantes / Android Authority

The serious cleaning hardware includes the FlowWash system, which uses a treadmill-style mop, 140-degree water, and 12N of downward pressure to scrub hard floors, while AI DirtSense adjusts the cleaning intensity based on how dirty they are. There’s also 31,000Pa of suction, CarpetFocus technology, and a DualFlow brush system designed to prevent hair tangles.

The smart features are equally impressive. Its NarMind™ Pro system and TwinAI™ Dodge obstacle avoidance use dual RGB cameras and AI to navigate around household clutter, with dedicated Baby Care and Pet Care modes. The dock handles hot-water self-cleaning and hot-air drying, and can automatically empty the dust for up to 120 days. You can get the Flow 2 in Pure White or Black.

Sony WH-1000XM6 for $348

Sony WH-1000XM6 Headphones

Sony WH-1000XM6 Headphones

The next iteration of the best Sony headphones

The Sony WH-1000XM6 is every bit a worthy successor to Sony's other ANC headphones as you'd hope. They sound very good, have excellent ANC, and are equipped to handle demanding users. However, the lack of cutting-edge connection options might be an issue as the years go by.

See price at Amazon

Save $111.99

Black Friday deal: $348 at Amazon (save $112).

Sony’s flagship noise canceling headphones are down to the lowest price Amazon itself has charged. The WH-1000XM6 builds on one of the most popular headphone lines around with stronger noise cancellation, a 12-microphone array for clearer calls, and the return of a foldable design that makes them easier to travel with. Sound quality is rich and detailed out of the box, with plenty of EQ control in Sony’s app, and you get up to 30 hours of playback with noise canceling switched on. All four colors are currently at this price.

SPONSORED

RayNeo iO Smart Glasses — $389 (22% off)

RayNeo iO Smart Glasses

RayNeo iO Smart Glasses

Camera-free AI glasses with an invisible heads-up display.

RayNeo iO puts an AI assistant and an invisible heads-up display into frames that look like everyday designer glasses. There's no camera, the frame is IP54 rated, and navigation, live translation and AI answers sit right in your line of sight.

Get the RayNeo iO now

Save $110.00

Black Friday deal: $389 (down from $499) until November 30 on Amazon and rayneo.com.

RayNeo iO is the easiest way to put a working AI assistant with an invisible display into your daily life, and this Black Friday it’s $389, down from $499, with a free six-month AI Pro VIP membership included. The glasses look like a stylish pair of everyday designer frames, and the micro-optical heads-up display is invisible to the person sitting across from you.

RayNeo

They’re also completely camera-free. There’s no lens and no recording of any kind, which makes them as easy to wear at dinner or in a meeting as any other pair of glasses — and everyone around you can see that at a glance.

They’re built for daily wear, too. The frame, hinges, and temples are engineered to an IP54 dust and water resistance rating, so a sudden downpour or a dusty trail isn’t something you need to plan around.

Two AI engines come built in, and neither needs a subscription: RayNeo V1 handles instant voice responses, while Google Gemini 3.1 Flash Lite provides contextual reasoning and ambient visual assistance. Those are standard on the glasses and stay yours regardless of what you do about a membership.

RayNeo

The free six-month AI Pro VIP membership then adds hands-free access to frontier models—ChatGPT 5.5, Gemini 3.1 Pro, DeepSeek V4 Pro, Qwen 3.7 Max, and Kimi K2.7—for live translation, deep reasoning, and everyday productivity. It applies to any iO bought between November 19 and November 30, and unlocks automatically when you activate the glasses by December 18, 2026.

Navigation is the feature you’ll reach for most. Directional arrows, street names, and live transit alerts sit in your natural line of sight, so your phone stays in your pocket wherever you walk or cycle.

There’s an extra reason to watch the second half of the sale if you wear prescription lenses. From November 27 to 30, base custom lenses are free on prescription-ready configurations — a $159 value — which means a prescription-equipped iO costs the same $389 as the standard pair, and upgraded lenses are free for the first 100 orders worldwide. If you want the dedicated portable charging case, the bundle is $428, down from $549.

And they keep getting better. RayNeo ships regular over-the-air updates, and the RayNeo iO SDK goes public in December 2026 — built so that people with no programming experience can create, upload, and share apps for the glasses. You describe what you want and build it by asking, which opens the door to unprecedented software: a recipe app that holds the next step in your eyeline while your hands are covered in flour, a reader that keeps your book above the handlebars, a custom tutorial for a specific hands-free task, a pace display for your morning run. You’ll also be able to wire up your own AI assistants and connect to third-party Bluetooth devices.

That’s the real case for buying in at $389 on Amazon or rayneo.com. The hardware is ready today — stylish, camera-free, and built to be worn in any weather — and the software is about to be handed to anyone with an idea and a sentence to describe it. These are glasses that become more valuable with every week you own them.

Lenovo Googlebook 15

Lenovo Googlebook 15

See price at Best Buy

Save $100.00

Googlebooks are barely out of the gate, but our readers have already picked a favorite. Lenovo’s Googlebook 15 came out on top in our recent poll of the five launch models, and its hardware goes some way toward explaining why. Better still, Best Buy has knocked $100 off the price for Black Friday, bringing this Android-based laptop down to $999.

Lenovo’s pitch is “Built to move at the speed of you. Simplify your day with Lenovo Googlebook 15 powered by Intel® Core™ Ultra 5 Series 3 processor.” That chip is paired with 16GB of RAM and 512GB of storage, but the big attraction might be the screen. You get a 15.3-inch 3K OLED touchscreen with a smooth 120Hz refresh rate, plus four Dolby Atmos speakers. That makes it a great option for watching a movie once you’re done being productive. And despite the large display, the laptop weighs less than three pounds.

Lenovo

Naturally, much of the excitement around Googlebooks is about the software. Gemini features include Magic Pointer, which can help you add calendar dates from whatever you’re looking at onscreen, and Rambler, which tidies up dictated thoughts. You can also access compatible apps and files from your Android phone, potentially saving you plenty of back-and-forth between devices.

There are a few other Best Buy perks worth knowing about. You can check whether your old laptop qualifies for trade-in, while selected accessories and networking products are available at 25% off with eligible purchases. Best Buy also includes six months of Webroot security software and a full year of Google AI Pro at no extra cost.

Nothing Phone (3) for $499

Nothing Phone 3

Nothing Phone 3

Nothing's first 'true flagship.'

The Phone 3 is a stylish reinvention of Nothing's Android phone series, now with flagship specs, including a large silicon-carbon battery, a Qualcomm Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 chipset, and a periscope zoom lens with macro photography support.

See price at Amazon

Save $200.00

Nothing’s flagship phone is back down to its lowest price, knocking $200 off the 256GB model. The Phone (3) stands out for its transparent design and the Glyph Matrix display on the back, which can show notifications, timers, and more without waking the screen. It’s no style-over-substance device, though: you get a Snapdragon 8s Gen 4 chip, a bright AMOLED display, four 50MP cameras, and a 5,150mAh battery, all running Nothing’s clean and thoughtful take on Android. Need more space? The 512GB model is also $200 off at $599.

Aurzen ZIP Pro x Jean-Michel Basquiat Special Edition Bundle

Handhelds are great for gaming on the go, but that little screen isn’t ideal when you want to play with friends. The Aurzen ZIP Pro offers a handy alternative, letting you project your games onto a much bigger surface without needing a TV. Its compact tri-fold body fits in a jacket pocket, yet delivers native 1080p projection. It connects directly to a Nintendo Switch over USB-C, with a dedicated Game Mode offering 20-40ms latency.

It’s also useful beyond gaming and movie nights. For example, sewing enthusiasts can project digital patterns onto a worktable instead of printing and taping together pages. The standard ZIP Pro is down to $579.99 (regularly $629.99) through November 30. Early buyers can also score a free GoPlay Portable Carrying Case or Z-Stand.

Aurzen

For sewing projects, the foldable design makes it easier to aim the projection onto your worktable, while ToF autofocus and four-point keystone correction help get the lines sharp and aligned. Wireless mirroring and USB-C projection from compatible devices give you options for displaying your patterns. For more conventional viewing, the built-in battery offers up to 2.5 hours in ECO Mode, and two people can listen privately using Bluetooth headphones.

There’s also a more eye-catching option for art lovers. The ZIP Pro x Jean-Michel Basquiat Special Edition Bundle offers the same projector with Basquiat-inspired artwork, two exclusive custom shells, special packaging, a MagPlay Pro and Z-Stand mounting setup, a custom GoPlay case, and a custom lens-cleaning cloth. It’s $649.99 in the sale (regularly $679.99).

Aurzen is also running a sitewide Black Friday draw through November 30, giving customers who order a chance to get their purchase for free. The results and winners will be announced on Aurzen’s official Instagram and Facebook accounts.

SPONSORED

Waterdrop M6CG countertop RO system — $388.55 (save $150)

Waterdrop M6CG Hot & Cold Countertop RO System

Waterdrop M6CG Hot & Cold Countertop RO System

The Waterdrop M6CG Countertop RO System is an installation-free water purifier with 8-stage reverse-osmosis filtration, remineralization, and instant hot and cold water. It offers adjustable temperatures, a detachable glass pitcher, and a 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio.

See price at Amazon

Save $150.45

Black Friday deal: $388.55 on Amazon with code AA26BFCM (save $150.45).

A water filter might not be top of your tech wishlist, but the Waterdrop M6CG certainly impressed our own Edgar Cervantes. After spending a few weeks testing it, he liked it so much that he moved it next to his desk and declared that it had genuinely improved his daily life — hence the Android Authority recommendation. Better still, Black Friday has brought the M6CG down to $409 from $539 on Amazon. Use our exclusive code AA26BFCM at checkout from November 19 through November 30 to bring it down to $388.55.

Waterdrop

The M6CG is a 2026 countertop reverse osmosis system, meaning no plumbing work or permanent installation is required. That’s a big plus if you’re renting, short on kitchen space, or want something for an office or RV. Its eight-stage filtration system removes impurities from tap water before adding minerals back to improve the taste.

More unusually, it handles both hot and cold water, with temperatures ranging from 59 to 203 degrees. That means the same machine can provide chilled water for a refreshing drink or piping-hot water for your morning coffee. Five dispensing volumes and a customizable Favorite Mode let you save your preferred temperature and quantity, while the detachable 40 oz glass pitcher is handy for serving guests, cooking, or keeping water in the fridge.

Separate tap-water and wastewater compartments prevent the two from mixing, while its efficient 3:1 pure-to-drain ratio means three parts filtered water for every part discarded. You can even reuse the wastewater for household cleaning or watering suitable plants. It’s a premium purchase, but the convenience of having mineral-enriched hot and cold water on demand makes it an attractive option.

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra

Powerful flagship with top-tier cameras, AI, and privacy features.

The Galaxy S26 Ultra is Samsung's slimmest and lightest Ultra yet, pairing a 6.9-inch display with the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 for Galaxy and a redesigned cooling system. It doubles down on imaging with a brighter 200MP main camera, upgraded zoom, advanced 8K video features, and Ultra-exclusive privacy and Galaxy AI tools.

See price at Amazon

SPONSORED

Vocci Ring for up to 35% off, plus three months of Vocci Pro

Vocci Ring — Save up to 35%

Vocci Ring — Save up to 35%

See price at Manufacturer site

Save $80.00

Black Friday deal: Save up to 35%, with three months of Vocci Pro included, from November 26 to 30 at Vocci.

The Vocci Ring is a wearable AI note-taker. It records your meetings so you can focus on the conversation and remember what was agreed. It’s made of titanium and weighs just a few grams, so it’s comfortable to wear all day.

Vocci

To start recording, simply double-click the ring — there’s no need to take out your phone. A single click lets you mark an important moment, like a deadline or an important number. You’ll get a quick confirmation with a small light and a gentle vibration. The ring records for up to eight hours on a single charge, and the charging case can recharge it about three times.

Once everything is synced, you can open the Vocci app to view the transcript, summary, and to-dos. So, if a client asks you to revise the budget and timeline in their proposal, you can revisit the meeting notes to see exactly what they requested. Then, you can use Vocci AI to draft a response and, of course, make any edits you’d like before sending it.

And with Vocci Desktop, you can easily add notes to your online meetings. Your calls and synced Ring sessions are all saved in the same Vocci account, so you can find everything in one convenient place.

The Vocci Ring is a great fit for anyone with a busy schedule of client meetings, sales calls, and team check-ins. It’s available in two finishes, usually priced at $249 and $299. From November 26 to November 30, you can get $30 off each model during Vocci’s Black Friday sale, bringing the price down to $219 or $269. Every purchase during the sale also includes three free months of Vocci Pro.

Get up to 35% off and three months of Vocci Pro through November 30.

Google Pixel Watch 5

Google Pixel Watch 5

The Google Pixel Watch 5 is a premium smartwatch with a brighter 3,000-nit AMOLED display, Snapdragon W5 Gen 2 processor, and advanced Gemini-powered assistance, alongside improved GPS, breathing emergency detection, blood pressure trend monitoring, and up to 40 hours of battery life in the 45mm model.

Battery life stretches to around 30 hours with the always-on display enabled, and you get Google’s full suite of health, sleep, and workout tracking built in. This price applies to the Obsidian Wi-Fi model.

Botslab G980H 4-Channel Dashcam — 30% off

Botslab G980H 4-Channel Dashcam

Botslab G980H 4-Channel Dashcam

Excellent image quality and a plethora of safety features

The Botslab Dash Cam G980H offers premium features with a Sony IMX 415 sensor recording in 4K and a 170-degree front view, plus a 1080p rear camera with a 150-degree view. It excels in low light with an f/1.5 aperture. Safety alerts, GPS tracking, and even parking mode round up a great product.

Save $89.50

Black Friday deal: $180.49 (33% off, saving $89.50) with code BOTSLABBF until December 31 on Amazon.

The Botslab G980H 4-Channel dashcam records the road ahead, traffic behind, and both sides of your car, all at the same time. This gives you peace of mind on the road and provides clear footage for your insurer or the police if they need to understand how an accident happened. It can be especially helpful in heavy traffic, on multi-lane roads, and in busy parking lots.

Botslab

The front camera records in 3K, while three 1080p cameras cover the rear and both sides. The two side cameras attach magnetically, so you can set them up and remove them quickly. You can use all four cameras, switch to three, or keep things simple with just the front and rear cameras. In the supported 3- and 2-channel modes, the front camera can also record in 4K for a little extra detail on the road ahead.

You’re covered even after you park. Pairing it with a compatible hardwire kit (sold separately) adds three helpful parking features. Sentry Mode starts recording when it detects motion around your vehicle, while collision detection captures footage if your car is hit. And with time-lapse recording, it condenses hours of parked time into a short video that’s easy to review.

The main unit features a 3.18″ touchscreen that makes setup and playback easy. Recordings appear in a convenient four-way split screen, letting you compare feeds from all the cameras at once. You can also take a photo or start recording with a voice command, while keeping both hands on the wheel.

Built-in GPS records your driving alongside your footage. You can download videos over the 5.8GHz Wi-Fi connection through the Botslab app, and a 128GB memory card is included, so you’ll have plenty of storage from the start.

The G980H 4-channel dashcam is a great choice if you’d like a comprehensive view around your car, with the flexibility to use just a couple of cameras if you don’t need all four. It’s also a great gift for someone who drives a lot for work, often parks on the street, or has a long holiday road trip coming up.

Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED

Garmin Instinct 3 AMOLED

That’s the real case for buying in at $389 on Amazon or rayneo.com. items.title: Motorola’s Android 17 update fixes Android Auto connections on folded Razr phones
items.summary: No more flipping open your Razr every time you start your car.
items.body:

Mobile

Motorola's Android 17 update fixes Android Auto connections on folded Razr phones

No more flipping open your Razr every time you start your car.

•

Nov 25, 2026 — 8:18 AM ET

•

•

Ryan Haines / Android Authority

Add Android Authority on Google:

Preferred Source

Google Discover

TL;DR

• Motorola Razr owners report that the Android 17 update fixes a long-standing Android Auto connectivity bug.

• The issue emerged after the Android 16 update, forcing affected users to unfold their phones to establish a connection.

One convenience of owning a flip phone is being able to carry out everyday tasks without unfolding it. But for some Motorola Razr owners, even something as simple as connecting to Android Auto has required opening their phones since the Android 16 update. Thankfully, the latest Android 17 update appears to be putting an end to this frustration.

A Motorola Razr Ultra 2025 owner took to Reddit to share that Android Auto is once again connecting automatically while their phone is folded shut following the Android 17 update. Other owners in the thread have reported similar improvements.

The problem dates back several months. In February, a Razr Plus 2024 owner reported that their phone used to connect to their car wirelessly without even taking it out of their pocket. After installing Android 16, they had to flip open the phone every time they started their car. Neither changing Android Auto’s settings nor clearing app data and reinstalling updates helped. The phone didn’t even need to be unlocked for Android Auto to start working again. Simply unfolding it was enough.

Connectivity isn’t the only issue flip phone owners have experienced with Google’s driving platform. In September, we reported on a separate Android Auto bug that prevented Motorola Razr and Samsung Galaxy Z Flip owners from making outgoing calls through Gemini while their phones were folded shut.

It’s unclear whether Motorola’s Android 17 update addresses that problem, too. Nevertheless, it’s encouraging to see Razr owners regain some of the convenience they lost with Android 16, especially for a feature they potentially use every day.
